Q: What are the best practices for high-speed differential pair routing in 4-layer PCBs A:

Answer 1： The linewidth and spacing of DDR3 clock differential pairs should be calculated using a two-dimensional field solver based on the actual stack-up, dielectric thickness, copper thickness, and FR-4 dielectric constant, to obtain a 100 Ω differential impedance, rather than using fixed empirical values.

Answer 2：Differential vias should be arranged in pairs and symmetrically, maintaining the same via diameter, pads, and anti-pad structure; ground return vias should be provided at layer transition points to reduce impedance discontinuities and common-mode conversion.

Answer 3：Differential clock lines should avoid being routed parallel to high-speed signals or noise sources for long distances. A spacing rule of 3W to 5W can be considered in the design （This is a High-Speed ​​PCB Design Guidelines：https://www.ultralibrarian.com/2026/03/03/high-speed-pcb-design-guidelines-ulc%EF%BC%89.

Answer 4：This webpage might be helpful to you. This discusses the related topics of tolerances for DDR3 trace matching. (https://electronics.stackexchange.com/questions/227968/tolerances-for-ddr3-trace-matching)

Answer 5：Relevant manufacturers’ design guidelines may be consulted, and additional support may be obtained from literature indexed in Web of Science or Scopus.

Q: SOQL query to get all accounts where none of related contact has useful information A:

You want:

  • Accounts that have contacts (so not "widows", Accounts that don't have any contacts)
  • But all of these contacts must be empty-ish (no phone, no email...)

You can make it happen with "semi joins" and "anti joins"

Sample uses of semi-joins and anti-joins include:

  • Get all contacts for accounts that have an opportunity with a particular record type.
  • Get all open opportunities for accounts that have active contracts.
  • Get all open cases for contacts that are the decision maker on an opportunity.
  • Get all accounts that don’t have any open opportunities.
SELECT Id, Name 
FROM Account
WHERE
    Id IN (SELECT AccountId FROM Contact)
    AND Id NOT IN (SELECT AccountId FROM Contact WHERE Email != null OR Phone != null)

    AND Malm__c = true
    AND typ_av_konto__c = 'Brf/Bf'
    AND e_post__c = null

In the SF sample data (you know, the kind you can find in Developer Edition, Trailhead playgrounds etc; "GenePoint", "Burlington Textiles", "University of Arizona"...) without your custom fields this query returns "sForce". Looks good, there are 2 contacts but they're poor quality all right:

If you consider "widows" interesting too (accounts that have poor quality contacts and accounts that have no contacts at all) - drop the Id IN (SELECT AccountId FROM Contact) AND part.

Q: npm ERR! code ENOTEMPTY npm ERR! syscall rename while trying to install Expo for react native A:

If on Mac or unix system, you can fix it by..

remove permissions: sudo -s

go to the directory it tells you in the error, like:

cd /usr/local/lib/node_modules/expo-cli

then remove the file: rm -r /usr/local/lib/node_modules/expo-cli

then try installing it again.

npm install -g expo-cli

Q: Windows command line for Disk Space usage report - sub directory level A:

You should be able to write a custom PowerShell, VBScript, or JScript solution easily enough.

Or you could use my JREN.BAT utility - a hybrid JScript/batch script that is designed to rename files/folders via regular expressions, but it has a /LIST option that can be used to provide custom directory listings. JREN.BAT is pure script that runs natively on any Windows machine from XP onward.

Assuming you have JREN.BAT somewhere within your PATH, then the following command will list folders on the D:\ drive that are at least 1000000000 bytes (decimal GB) in size. Note that the reported size of each folder includes the size of all its children. So if a child is greater than 1GB, then its parent is guaranteed to also be greater than 1GB.

jren "^.*" "lpad((size()/1000000000).toFixed(3),'        ')+'  '+path()" /s /d /j /list /p "D:\" | findstr /rvc:"^ *0"

The JREN command lists each foder size in GB, followed by the full path. I pipe that to FINDSTR to filter out folders that are smaller than 1GB.

Given that JREN.BAT is a bat file, you must prefix the command with CALL if you want to use it in a batch script.

There are lots of options to specify the root path, exclusion lists, path masks, etc. Full documentation is embedded within the utility.

I believe there is a bug in the current version that causes the command to fail when it tries to access the size of a folder that it does not have access to. I may fix that when I get a chance.

Q: .NET Core add Web Reference A:
  • Select old project in Solution Explorer.
  • Click 'Show All Files' button Solution Explorer toolbar.
  • Service node will be expanded and you will see the nested nodes with generated code.
  • You should find the link to WSDL file, which describes your web service.
  • To load a service metadata from a WSDL file, select Browse in Add Web Reference dialog.

Documentation states:

The WCF Web Service Reference tool retrieves metadata from a web service in the current solution, on a network location, or from a WSDL file, and generates a source file containing Windows Communication Foundation (WCF) client proxy code that your .NET app can use to access the web service.
